mentalMap.label: The four questions
mentalMap.sub: who runs it, who pays, where value lands, what is tokenised — every model in this unit is a different answer to these

mentalMap.label: Why a model is needed
mentalMap.sub: running costs, the payer, the free rider, the contribution incentive, governance, review

mentalMap.label: The classical base
mentalMap.sub: subscription, licence, marketplace, freemium, services — each breaks where the trust used to sit

mentalMap.label: The taxonomy
mentalMap.sub: BaaS and platform (infrastructure), marketplace (trades), software (code), services (expertise), P2P (token) — each with its own risk

mentalMap.label: BaaS in detail
mentalMap.sub: provider runs nodes, consensus, keys, monitoring, upgrades, SLA; customer keeps contracts, data model, integrations

mentalMap.label: Token economy
mentalMap.sub: classify, cap, distribute, give it a job, route the value, burn the fee, check the legal test

mentalMap.label: Utility token loop
mentalMap.sub: service needs token → token needs scarcity → token must pay the real cost, else the loop is open

mentalMap.label: Software product
mentalMap.sub: sell the brush not the painting — customer runs the chain, you collect the licence

mentalMap.label: P2P
mentalMap.sub: no take-rate; the coordinator is paid by the ecosystem, not by the trade

mentalMap.label: Professional services
mentalMap.sub: advisory, integration, managed ops — charge for the kitchen, not the wrenching

mentalMap.label: Banking and settlement
mentalMap.sub: correspondent chain → shared ledger; atomic DVP kills PvP risk, back office moves rather than disappears

topExamQuestions: Explain the types of blockchain business model (BaaS, marketplace, platform/infrastructure, software products, professional services and P2P), compare them, and identify the model a named company is running. (15 marks)
What is Blockchain as a Service? Explain what the provider actually runs and what the customer keeps, and why it is the default entry point for enterprises. (15 marks)
Explain the token economy: token classification (utility, security, commodity), supply and distribution, value accrual, and the regulatory line between utility and investment. (15 marks)
Explain how a blockchain can be applied to banking and financial transactions — settlement, PvP risk, atomic DVP, KYC/AML and the real cost model for a bank's back office. (15 marks)
Define a blockchain business model and explain it in terms of the four questions every such model must answer. (5 marks)
Explain the utility token business model and the demand loop, and the conditions under which it breaks down. (5 marks)
Why does a shared ledger need an explicit business model, and what happens to a consortium when nobody pays for the ledger? (5 marks)
Compare the traditional business models with blockchain business models and say where each breaks down. (5 marks)
Explain the blockchain-based software product model and how it differs from BaaS. (5 marks)
Explain the P2P blockchain business model and how the coordinator earns from the network rather than from the transactions. (5 marks)
Explain the three lines of blockchain professional services and the pitfall of selling hours instead of an outcome. (5 marks)
drill: What are the four questions of a blockchain business model?
Who runs it, who pays, where value accrues, what is tokenised
Does a blockchain business model need a token?
No — tokenisation is a choice; software and services models tokenise nothing
What does a BaaS provider run?
Nodes, consensus, key custody, monitoring, upgrades and the SLA
Who holds the keys in BaaS?
The provider — that is the largest trust transfer in the arrangement
What does the customer keep in BaaS?
Its business logic, data model and integrations
What is the single question that classifies all blockchain business models?
Where the money comes from
Name the six models and one risk each
BaaS=operating, platform=ecosystem, marketplace=liquidity, software=adoption, services=capacity, P2P=token
Marketplace vs P2P — the one-line difference?
Marketplace takes a cut of the trades; the P2P coordinator takes no cut
What are the three token types?
Utility, security, commodity-like — set by the claim the token makes
What are the four variables of a token economy?
Total supply, distribution, utility demand, value accrual
Where is the regulatory line drawn?
Whether buyers expect returns from the efforts of others (Howey / SEBI CIS)
Name the four routes of value accrual
Fee burn, fee sharing to stakers, staking rewards, shrinking supply
State the utility token demand loop
Service → token needed → token spent/burned → network grows → more users → more demand
What breaks the utility loop?
Unlimited free utility, a fee below the node's real cost, or users routing around the token
What is PvP risk?
One leg of a trade settles while the other does not
How does atomic DVP remove it?
Both legs commit in the same transaction, so both succeed or both fail
What happens to a bank's back office on a shared ledger?
It moves — reconciliation becomes on-chain verification; KYC/AML, keys and nodes are new costs
Where does blockchain settlement fit best?
High-value multi-party cross-border flows, not small retail payments
Three professional services lines?
Advisory, integration, managed operations
The services trap?
Selling hours caps income at the number of billable people
What is the free-rider problem?
Everyone values the shared record, everyone under-contributes to it
Software product vs BaaS — one line?
In BaaS the provider runs the chain; in software the customer does
